timing_gold.scope: Stage ceilings for the EH plan-check segment only. The Building & Safety segment (A12, A16) is run by 85+ separate city building departments and has no county-level clock at all.
timing_gold.staleness_warning: D8's cadence and staffing numbers are from 1999. Treat the six-month interval as structural evidence that a routine cycle exists, not as a current interval.

known_gaps: No measured plan-check turnaround, backlog, or queue depth for LA County. The 20/10-business-day figures are ceilings; nothing in the corpus reports what actually happens.
Current inspector staffing and vacancy rate: unknown. The only figure in the whole corpus ('authorized to fund 140 inspectors... Not all positions are always filled') is from 1999.
Whether the internal reviewer checklist matches the 'complete plan' list published in D6 cannot be verified from outside; D6 itself concedes interpretation is left to each jurisdiction.
The dollar amount of the 'additional fees... for corrections due to scope changes or incomplete work' (A09) is not in D1 or D7.
The meaning of the '(OII)' fee rows in D7 (RESTAURANT LOW/MOD/HIGH RISK (OII), $330-$440) is never explained in any captured document.
Current adoption status of Ordinance 97-0071 across LA County's 88 cities is unknown; only the 1999 snapshot survives (51 adopted, 6 rejected, 3 residential-only cities not applicable).
AB 671 took effect 2026-01-01 and D6 is dated February 2026, so no post-implementation evidence exists on whether the resubmittal/change-of-scope taxonomy changed outcomes.

Mobile food facilities are out of scope here; LA runs a separate commissary-gated MFF track with its own random commissary-use verification inspections (see lac_mobile_plan_check.txt). A separate gold model would be needed.

Scope boundary for disentanglement scoring: MEHKO, cottage food (Class A/B) and community-event temporary food facilities are separate LA County tracks with their own fee codes and application deadlines (D5, D7), not variants of this process.

D1's saved .txt interleaves the flowchart's three columns line-by-line. Quotes here reflect box text (reproducible with `pdftotext -raw`). A solver reading only the .txt faces a genuine extraction obstacle — which is itself a realistic condition, not a defect to fix in the gold.
notes: Why this LA model has only 3 staff_only activities while the SF model has 6: LA County publishes an unusual amount of its own procedure. D4 is written in the staff imperative ('Health inspectors will: ... Wash their hands prior to commencing the inspection') and includes the compliance-date rule table, so the whole inspection sequence that would be an SOP elsewhere is public here. What remains genuinely invisible in LA is not sequence but *capacity and jurisdiction*: which of 21 districts a facility lands in (A20), how the routine cycle is rationed against unfilled inspector positions (A21), and whether the letter-grade ordinance even applies in the city the facility sits in (A28). Two structural contrasts worth scoring against the SF model: (1) LA's EH plan check is a direct, separate submittal to the health department, and the EH final inspection is deliberately sequenced *after* all city Building & Safety approvals ('you must obtain all approvals from your local building and safety office prior to your final inspection with EH Plan Check'), whereas SF folds DPH review inside the single DBI Permit Center submittal; (2) LA sells a queue position — the expedited tier costs about 1.5x and halves the review ceiling — a fact no LA page states in words and that is only recoverable by reading D1's timing line against D7's fee rows. The sharpest mandated/designed seam is A09: HSC 114380(f) as amended by AB 671 says only 'resubmittal', and LA County invented the resubmittal-vs-change-of-scope taxonomy, with worked examples, to operationalise it — San Diego County independently published a near-identical taxonomy, which the public record cannot distinguish from shared CDPH/CCDEH guidance.
